about: Pieces any theme uses: saved parts (chests, spawners, treasure), lights and props that fit anywhere.
made_by: tools/dungeons/palette_tool.py (curation in CURATED there; everything else read from the game's files)

fields.role: what it's for; structural roles (arch, block, ceiling, door, floor, gate, pillar, platform, rail, ramp, stair, wall) must be solid
fields.mount: ground: stands on a floor (prop_check.py); hang: needs something right above its origin or a chain on its top; wall: against a wall; span: rests on two supports; structure: what others stand on; free: anywhere
fields.scale: [min, max] that looks right and stays solid; stairs keep 1 (step height)
fields.tier: the land it looks like it belongs to (1 Meadows .. 8 Deep North): a look hint, not gameplay (enemies and loot follow the entrance's biome)
fields.size/min/max/origin: its shape's box in its own frame (m); origin: where its origin sits on that box (foot, top, centre...)
fields.solid: a character bumps into it in our rooms (the game's collision matrix; items fixed by BuildSolid.cs)
fields.lights: range, intensity, colour; lit: shines once stripped (a Fireplace's burning objects are switched on); lod: fades with distance
fields.gives: what the game would make it give or do: stripped as scenery; a networked prefab (networked) may be a Saved part instead
fields.climb: ledges: its footholds (faces a player can stand on, no steeper than 38 degrees, with at least 0.1 m2 of them seen from above in a 0.2 m height band) as height ranges above its foot at scale 1, upright as the prefab stands; top: the highest reachable from the floor, each within a jump (1.6 m: gravity 20, jump force 8, Jump skill 0) of the last; top_skilled: the same with Jump skill 100 (3.14 m); 0: none. Scale the ledges by the part's y scale; a part turned off upright exposes other faces (treat a smooth bar or column as only its top end)
fields.upright: flat (thin along y: a floor tile, stand it up for a wall), upright (thin along x or z: a wall piece, use as it is), block
fields.safe: fine as stripped scenery; saved_only: works only as a Saved part (chests, pickables, spawners)
fields.by_role: {role: [default, variants...]}: the roles below without their notes
fields.sets: the dressing sets it suits (giant: ossuary, ruin, forge, archive, engine, armoury; Dvergr: store, workshop, tavern, barracks)
fields.max_span: a panel's longest side (m) before its stretched texture smears
fields.roles: the same pieces by a theme recipe's roles (first = default, others = variants), with how each role's pieces are placed
fields.render: a picture in the mesh cache (C:\Users\DHack\AppData\Local\Temp\quaddungeon_meshes); the theme's contact sheet is palettes/shared_sheet.png there

trouble.Morkhalla_MetalPillar: not in the game's ZNetScene (it's only part of Mórk halla rooms): dungeon_parts.py refuses it. Use Piece_flametal_pillar or Morkhalla_MetalBar stood up.
trouble.CharredCogwheel: an item prefab: players walked through the giant gears (its collider is a 1.14 x 0.4 x 1.14 box on the 'item' layer). The Builder now moves it to static_solid and fits a disc collider (BuildSolid.cs). Never Saved: it would be an Ashlands item.
trouble.dvergrprops_lantern: floated in the first Shifting Halls (hanging lanterns with nothing above): hang it from a beam, a ceiling or dvergrprops_hooknchain / Morkhalla_WallChain1 with the chain's foot on its top (prop_check.py).
trouble.piece_brazierceiling01: hangs: needs a ceiling or beam right above its origin.
trouble.dverger_guardstone: a ward (PrivateArea): stripped it's only a look, but it reads as a player's ward. Don't use.
trouble.MistArea: the Mistlands mist: it hides everything around it in a dungeon. Don't use (also MistArea_small, MistArea_edge).
trouble.Morkhalla_Rubble1_fall: falls (physics) in the game: stripped it's frozen mid-air. Use Morkhalla_Rubble1.
trouble.dverger_demister: floated in 35 places in Shifting Halls: its origin is at its top (the mesh hangs below it), so stood at a point it's in the air. Hang it on a chain from the first part above it (giant_kit.wisp).
trouble.dvergrprops_banner: its origin is in its middle (2 m above its foot): stood at a point it reaches 2 m higher than it seems, and left a 6 m room's box.
trouble.blackmarble_2x2x1: stretched, its bevels become spikes: don't use it as a stretched wall (blackmarble_tile_wall_2x4 instead).
trouble.Ashlands_floor_large_fractured: looks the same as Ashlands_floor_large: no use for a cracked floor.
trouble.giant_ribs: huge (0.75 scale is still about 14 m long), and hollow: its collider is boxes in prefab_shapes.json. Scale giant remains by their box.
trouble.*_frac: fractured debris (physics pieces of something broken): don't use as scenery.
trouble.Pickable_*: as scenery a pickable shows its item but can't be taken: confusing. Use only as Saved parts.
trouble.TreasureChest_*: as scenery a chest opens nothing: Saved only, scale 1.
trouble.Spawner_*: invisible and does nothing as scenery: Saved only.
